title: Microfluidic Modeling of Macrophage-Induced Cardiac Inflammation Using NF-kappaB Reporter Cardiomyocytes.
authors: Liu, Chao; Qiang Lu, Xi Rui; Jeong, Seoyoung; Wu, Douglas H; Somoza, Rodrigo A; Ramakrishnan, Parameswaran; Senyo, Samuel E
one_liner_zh: 该文用微流控芯片和NF-kB报告基因心肌细胞模拟巨噬细胞诱导的心脏炎症，虽涉及NF-kB转录因子信号，但核心是细胞共培养与炎症表型，无蛋白质-DNA互作建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: Inflammation is a key driver of cardiac disease progression, including heart failure and myocardial infarction, with macrophage-cardiomyocyte interactions playing a central role in shaping the local inflammatory microenvironment. Prolonged exposure to pro-inflammatory cytokines, many produced by macrophages, induces cardiomyocyte stress, dysfunction, and pathological tissue remodeling. However, the spatial and temporal dynamics of this crosstalk remain poorly understood, limiting the development of targeted therapies. To address this gap, we developed an in vitro cardiac inflammation model that enables controlled investigation of macrophage-cardiomyocyte interactions. Cardiomyocytes were transduced with an NF-kappaB-responsive fluorescent reporter to allow real-time monitoring of inflammatory signaling. MATLAB-based simulations were used to optimize medium delivery and cell densities by modeling TNFalpha diffusion. Using a multiplex microfluidic co-culture chip, we identified the TNFalpha threshold of 50 ng mL(-) (1) with a 6-h exposure as sufficient to activate cardiomyocyte NF-kappaB signaling. Both macrophage-conditioned medium and direct co-culture significantly increased NF-kappaB activation, indicating enhanced cardiomyocyte inflammatory stress. Dexamethasone markedly suppressed NF-kappaB activation when administered at onset of co-culture to both cell types, whereas IL-10 showed limited efficacy. Overall, this cardiac inflammation model provides a versatile platform for dissecting immune-cardiac crosstalk and supports future studies of multicellular crosstalk, spatiotemporal signaling dynamics, and therapeutic screening.
abstract_zh: 炎症是心脏疾病进展的关键驱动因素，包括心力衰竭和心肌梗死，其中巨噬细胞-心肌细胞相互作用在塑造局部炎症微环境中发挥核心作用。长期暴露于促炎细胞因子（其中许多由巨噬细胞产生）会诱导心肌细胞应激、功能障碍和病理性组织重塑。然而，这种相互作用的时空动态仍知之甚少，限制了靶向疗法的开发。为弥补这一空白，我们开发了一种体外心脏炎症模型，能够对巨噬细胞-心肌细胞相互作用进行受控研究。心肌细胞被转导了NF-kappaB响应性荧光报告基因，以实现炎症信号传导的实时监测。基于MATLAB的模拟通过建模TNFalpha扩散来优化培养基输送和细胞密度。利用多重微流控共培养芯片，我们确定了50 ng mL(-) (1)的TNFalpha阈值，且6小时暴露足以激活心肌细胞NF-kappaB信号传导。巨噬细胞条件培养基和直接共培养均显著增加NF-kappaB激活，表明心肌细胞炎症应激增强。地塞米松在共培养开始时对两种细胞类型给药，显著抑制了NF-kappaB激活，而IL-10显示出有限的效果。总体而言，该心脏炎症模型为解析免疫-心脏相互作用提供了一个多功能平台，并支持未来多细胞相互作用、时空信号动力学及治疗筛选的研究。
